definitions.explanation: A tall plant with large yellow flowers that turn to follow the sun.

examples.japanese: {向日葵|ひまわり}は{夏|なつ}の{花|はな}です。
{向日葵|ひまわり}は{大|おお}きくて{黄色|きいろ}い{花|はな}だ。
{向日葵|ひまわり}{畑|ばたけ}は{写真|しゃしん}スポットとして{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Sunflower fields are popular photo spots.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}に{向日葵|ひまわり}の{種|たね}をまいたら、{夏|なつ}にたくさん{花|はな}が{咲|さ}きました。
examples.english: When I planted sunflower seeds in the garden, many flowers bloomed in summer.

examples.japanese: {向日葵|ひまわり}{畑|ばたけ}は{夏|なつ}の{人気|にんき}の{写真|しゃしん}スポットで、{毎年|まいとし}{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{見|み}に{来|き}ます。
examples.english: Sunflower fields are popular photo spots in summer, and many people come to see them every year.

notes:
The name {向日葵|ひまわり} means 'facing the sun' ({向|む}く + {日|ひ} + {葵|あおい}), referring to the flower's heliotropic behavior (following the sun). Also written as ヒマワリ.

Symbolism:
- Summer ({夏|なつ}の{花|はな})
- Brightness, energy, vitality
- Admiration, loyalty (turning toward the sun)

Products from sunflowers:
- {向日葵|ひまわり}の{種|たね} (sunflower seeds - snack)
- ひまわり{油|あぶら} (sunflower oil)

Famous sunflower locations:
- {北海道|ほっかいどう}{北竜町|ほくりゅうちょう}
- Various {向日葵|ひまわり}{畑|ばたけ} (sunflower fields) across Japan

The 1970 film 「{ひまわり}」 (Sunflower) starring Sophia Loren features an iconic sunflower field scene shot in Ukraine.
